key_insight: A digital quantum computer can simulate real-time string dynamics in a (2+1)D U(1) quantum link model by encoding gauge fields in qubits, enabling experiments on confining behavior and quench-induced string fluctuations.
engineering_relevance: The work shows that hardware-aware lattice mapping plus error mitigation can make larger, gauge-theory dynamics simulations feasible on present-day IBM quantum devices.
method: Map dual height variables of a minimal U(1) quantum link model onto qubits.
Choose a lattice geometry compatible with IBM heavy-hex hardware to reduce long-range couplings.
Run quantum quenches from an initial string state and compare dynamics with tensor-network references.
evidence_signal: Experimental digital quantum simulations using up to 112 qubits matched tensor-network results at short times and thermal averages at long times, including near the phase transition after error mitigation.
watch_item: Local gauge-symmetry violations still arise from hardware noise, so results depend on mitigation quality and remain sensitive to finite-circuit and finite-bond-dimension effects in comparisons.
paper_title: String dynamics of a (2+1)D U(1) quantum link model on a digital quantum computer
